newsitem.title: UK: Peugeot UK workers accept new pay deal.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot UK workers accept new pay deal.

text.p: British workers at French car-maker PSA Peugeot's Coventry plant in England have voted in favour of a new pay deal and averted the threat of all-out-strike, unions said on Thursday.

The Transport and General Workers Union (T&G), involved in negotiations with the company over recent days, told Reuters that a ballot of workers had come out in favour of accepting the new offer. The vote showed 1,521 in favour of a new five percent rise in basic pay, with 563 against.
The Peugeot management's new offer also includes scrapping plans for the introduction of performance related pay and has increased lay-off pay.

Earlier this month the British workers had voted overwhelmingly in favour of strike action, due to start in April. They claimed they were among the lowest paid in the industry and resisted plans to alter shift patterns.

But Tony Woodley, chief negotiator for the motor industry at the T&G, warned Peugeot "The end of this dispute signals the beginning of an uneasy peace with Peugeot. No-one should underestimate the anger and frustration that our members still feel."
The dispute between the two sides has been rumbling on since December. Coventry makes 85,000 cars a year and is one of Peugeot's three European plants. The others are in Spain and France.
